To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
common variants in three genes that are known to be involved in breast cancer development are not involved in breast cancer survival.
common variants in ATM, CHEK, and ERBB genes are not associated with breast cancer survival or risk of breast tumors with certain characteristics.
common genetic variation in the genes ATM, CHEK 2 and ERBB 2 is not involved in modifying the risk of breast cancer survival or tumour characteristics.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
common genetic variation in the ERBB 2, CHEK2, and ATM genes does not play a major role in the risk of developing breast cancer or in the risk of dying from the disease.

the role of common variation in the ATM gene in breast cancer aetiopathogenesis is still unclear, whereas the role of CHEK2 and the ERBB2 genes seems to be limited to a small fraction of the population.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic variants we studied do not seem to have an important impact on breast cancer survival or tumour characteristics.
common variants in ATM, CHEK and ERBB2 are not associated with breast cancer risk, breast cancer survival and breast cancer tumour characteristics in a Swedish population.
the ATM and CHEK2 genes are not important in the aetiology of breast cancer in the general population, while the ERBB2 locus may be important in the aetiologies of some breast cancer subtypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of common variants in the development of cancer is likely to be small, at least in the case of ATM, CHEK and ERBB2.
common variation in the genes ATM, CHEK and ERBB2 does not have a role in the aetiology of breast cancer or the survival of breast cancer patients.
the role of these genes in breast tumour aetiology and progression should be further studied in larger studies.
